They are struggling to reconcile this social pressure with their own lack of certainty about whether they actually desire those outcomes.

minds.title: The Stoic
minds.concern: Distinguishing between what is in our control and what is not.
minds.author: Epictetus

minds.title: The Social Critic
minds.concern: The role of mimetic desire in shaping our goals through others.
minds.author: René Girard

minds.title: The Existentialist
minds.concern: The burden of radical freedom and the trap of bad faith.

debate.speaker: The Stoic
debate.text: You suffer because you have handed over your peace of mind to the opinions of others. If you desire what is not in your control, such as timing your life to match your friends, you will always be a slave to their choices.
debate.author: Epictetus

debate.speaker: The Social Critic
debate.text: It is not just about opinion, but about the structure of desire itself. We do not want things for their own sake; we want them because our models—our friends—want them. The feeling of being behind is the inevitable result of imitating their desires.
debate.author: René Girard
debate.basis: Basis: René Girard, Deceit, Desire, and the Novel

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: You are both missing the point. The user is in bad faith. By claiming to feel behind, they are pretending that there is a fixed path they have failed to walk, rather than admitting that they are entirely free to define their own existence.
debate.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Paul Sartre, Being and Nothingness

debate.speaker: The Stoic
debate.text: To be free, one must first recognize that external status is an indifferent. If the user finds no value in these milestones, why do they bother to label themselves as behind at all? That label is a judgment they are choosing to make.
debate.author: Epictetus

debate.speaker: The Social Critic
debate.text: It is difficult to simply choose otherwise when the entire social environment reinforces these goals. The user feels behind because they are caught in a mimetic triangle, where the desire of the other becomes the standard for their own self-worth.
debate.author: René Girard
debate.basis: Basis: René Girard, Deceit, Desire, and the Novel

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: But that is an excuse. To say the environment forces you is to deny your own agency. You are not a victim of the social circle; you are the one who continues to validate their values by measuring your life against them.
debate.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Paul Sartre, Being and Nothingness

debate.speaker: The Social Critic
debate.text: I see your point. I previously argued that the social pressure was the primary culprit, but you are right that the user is actively participating in this comparison. I now realize the problem is not the friends, but the user's reliance on them to define their own lack of purpose.
debate.author: René Girard
debate.basis: Basis: René Girard, Deceit, Desire, and the Novel

debate.speaker: The Stoic
debate.text: Exactly. If you remove the external comparison, you are left with your own character. If you find no joy in the house or the marriage, then you are not behind; you are simply on a different road. The only thing that matters is how you use your time.
debate.author: Epictetus

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: And that is the terrifying part. Once you realize the social path is not mandatory, you have no excuse for your inaction. You must choose what to value, and you must own that choice completely, without blaming the timing of your peers.
debate.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Paul Sartre, Being and Nothingness

output.clearer: The debate shifted from viewing the user as a victim of social pressure to seeing them as an active participant in their own distress. The insight is that the feeling of being behind is a choice to use others' lives as a yardstick for one's own, rather than creating a personal standard. What remains disputed is whether one can ever truly escape the influence of social mimesis or if we are always defining ourselves in relation to others.
output.dependsOn: If the user values social belonging above all else, then the feeling of being behind is a signal to align with their peers; if the user values personal autonomy, the feeling is a signal to stop measuring their life against external milestones and instead define their own. If the user is unsure of their values, they should experiment with small, non-milestone-related goals to see what actually generates a sense of fulfillment.
